findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that grandchildren 591d/8b08 (children of 2db2) carry every parent Portability AC (P1-P9) as a parseable observable, or lift the missing observables onto 2db2's own acceptance criteria so the direct-child roster covers them.
evidence: Parent portability ACs enumerate P1-P9 (scrubbed contract, shallow-clone f193, committed Jenkinsfile/.gitlab-ci.yml, 20-min GHA, shared exit/secret/timeout table, single-quoted Groovy, offline GitLab schema, shellcheck all three, shellcheck provisioning).

2db2 has only 7 ACs, none of which name Jenkinsfile, .gitlab-ci.yml, shellcheck, GitLab schema, secret/timeout table, single-quoted Groovy, shallow-clone rejection, or the 20-minute schedule; its runner AC only asserts execution 'through exactly rebar bridge run'.
2db2 Context/Plan: the portability observables are owned by two children (591d runner-neutral entrypoint + wrappers; 8b08 repair) that are NOT present in the supplied sibling roster.
No other roster sibling's ACs deliver P1-P9 (searched across all 12 children's indented criteria).
findings.finding: Nine parent Portability acceptance criteria have no covering acceptance criterion among the 12 direct children in the roster. The named coordinator (child 2db2) delegates them to grandchildren 591d/8b08, which are NOT in the sibling roster; 2db2's own seven ACs cover only child-closure, legacy retention, the packaged runner via `rebar bridge run`, and the no-gh repair test. The specific uncovered/indeterminate criteria are: scrubbed-environment identical contract failing on vendor-variable reads or required gh (P1), full-depth success + named shallow-clone rejection for bug f193 (P2), Jenkinsfile and .gitlab-ci.yml committed and doc-referenced (P3), GHA 20-minute production workflow (P4), one code-derived exit/secret/timeout table (P5), single-quoted Jenkins Groovy body (P6), offline GitLab schema validation with recorded provenance (P7), pinned shellcheck over all three providers (P8), and CI shellcheck provisioning with named-failure-not-skip (P9).
findings.location: child 2db2-3f5e-cf3a-464c (Acceptance Criteria) vs parent 'Portability acceptance criteria' P1-P9
scenarios: A completion verifier checking the parent's P1-P9 against the union of direct children's ACs finds no matching observable and cannot confirm coverage.

Reviewers relying only on the roster cannot verify the Jenkins single-quoting, GitLab offline schema, or shellcheck-provisioning contracts because their owning grandchildren are absent from the material under review.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit acceptance criteria to 2db2 (or surface 591d/8b08 in the roster) for each of P1-P9 so the union of direct children demonstrably delivers the scrubbed-env contract, shallow-clone rejection, committed+referenced Jenkinsfile/.gitlab-ci.yml, 20-min GHA, shared exit/secret/timeout table, single-quoted Groovy, offline GitLab schema validation, and pinned-shellcheck provisioning.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure a direct child (2db2 or a roster-visible child) carries the observable that bridge execution SUCCEEDS in each of local/GHA/Jenkins/GitLab/bare, not merely that all five route through `rebar bridge run`.
evidence: Parent main AC7: 'The bridge runs locally, on GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments.'

2db2 AC5 speaks to routing/entrypoint identity ('use the packaged Python core... through exactly rebar bridge run; no repository-local runner script is required'), which is a precursor to, not the same observable as, successful multi-environment execution.
The scrubbed-environment execution contract that would prove identical successful runs (portability P1) is not in any roster sibling's ACs.
findings.finding: Parent main AC7 ('The bridge runs locally, on GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments') is only partially covered by the roster. Child 2db2 AC5 asserts that these five environments 'use the packaged Python core in src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py through exactly rebar bridge run', but no direct-child AC in the roster demonstrates the OBSERVABLE outcome that a bridge run actually SUCCEEDS end-to-end in each of the five environments (that observable is delegated to grandchildren 591d/8b08 absent from the roster).
findings.location: child 2db2-3f5e-cf3a-464c (AC5) vs parent main AC 'The bridge runs locally, on GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, and bare environments'
scenarios: A verifier of main AC7 finds only a routing/entrypoint assertion in the roster, not proof that Jenkins/GitLab/bare runs succeed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to 2db2 an acceptance criterion asserting the scrubbed-environment success/identity contract (or surface 591d in the roster) so main AC7's five-environment run-success is delivered at the direct-child level.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record prior-art consideration for the extracted-bash shellcheck harness: name the existing multi-provider extractors (e.g. mschuett/yaml-shellcheck, gitlab-ci-verify, shellscan) and justify the bespoke 'polyglot lint' extension against them, or adopt one.
evidence: Plan frames the extractor as bespoke ('an extension of the polyglot bespoke lint').

Retrieved prior art: github.com/mschuett/yaml-shellcheck — 'Wrapper script to run shellcheck on YAML CI-config files ... GitLab CI, GitHub Actions' (exactly the multi-provider extraction the AC describes).
Retrieved prior art: github.com/coroboros/shellscan — 'lint every shell ... scripts embedded in GitLab CI and GitHub Actions YAML'; and timo-reymann/gitlab-ci-verify ShellCheck integration.
ABSENCE: the plan nowhere weighs these existing extractors against a hand-rolled one (no Rule-of-Three / anti-repackaging rationale).
findings.finding: The portability AC mandating a bespoke 'polyglot bespoke lint' extension that extracts and shellchecks bash bodies from all three CI providers reinvents an established, purpose-built tool class without considering or rejecting it.
findings.location: Portability acceptance criteria: 'Pinned shellcheck validates extracted bash bodies from all three providers. It is a required test-harness tool, not a runtime dependency or an extension of the polyglot bespoke lint.'
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer discovers the hand-rolled YAML-to-bash extractor duplicates yaml-shellcheck and must justify or replace it.
The bespoke extractor mishandles a provider YAML construct (matrix, anchors, multiline) that a mature tool already covers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile child 1c1b's D1/AC3 BRIDGE_ALERT premise with child 030f, which RETAINS the emitter; correct 1c1b's wording so its strict-mode 'no event' rationale does not assert a deletion 030f never performs.
evidence: 1c1b D1: 'that ticket DELETES the BRIDGE_ALERT emitter (dispatch_one.py:353), its reducer arm and _engine_support/bridge.py, on the evidence that 0 BRIDGE_ALERT events exist'

030f Context: 'the dispatch_one.py BRIDGE_ALERT event emitter is live on the create identity-write failure path, its reducer feeds TicketState.bridge_alerts... Those live paths are explicitly retained.'
030f AC: 'The live BRIDGE_ALERT event emitter and reducer remain covered and unchanged.'
Parent close comment confirms the conflict: '1c1b now corrects its stale D1 premise and states that 030f retained BRIDGE_ALERT.'
findings.finding: Child 1c1b's decision D1 rests on a premise that contradicts sibling 030f: 1c1b states that 030f 'DELETES the BRIDGE_ALERT emitter (dispatch_one.py:353), its reducer arm and _engine_support/bridge.py', whereas 030f's own context and acceptance criteria explicitly RETAIN it ('The live BRIDGE_ALERT event emitter and reducer remain covered and unchanged').
findings.location: child 1c1b-1da2-7ff4-4770 (Decisions D1); cross-referenced against child 030f-c14f-596a-4f79 (Decisions 1 and Context)
scenarios: A reader of 1c1b concludes the emitter is being removed and does not need coverage, while 030f keeps it live — the two children disagree on the disposition of the same emitter.
1c1b's AC3 ('Strict mode emits NO BRIDGE_ALERT event... so this ticket does not resurrect the emitter 030f deletes') is written against a deletion that 030f never performs.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend 1c1b D1 and AC3 to state that 030f retains the live BRIDGE_ALERT emitter and that strict mode simply adds no NEW alert artifact (process exit is the channel), rather than claiming the emitter is deleted.

findings.finding: Children 030f and 1c1b hold contradictory assumptions about whether 030f deletes the BRIDGE_ALERT event emitter/reducer. 030f's Context and Decisions explicitly RETAIN the live dispatch_one.py BRIDGE_ALERT emitter, its reducer, and the bridge_state/bridge_alerts JSONL channel (and has an AC: 'The live BRIDGE_ALERT event emitter and reducer remain covered and unchanged'). But 1c1b's Decision D1 is premised on the opposite: it states '030f decision 3 ... DELETES the BRIDGE_ALERT emitter (dispatch_one.py:353), its reducer arm and _engine_support/bridge.py' and designs strict-mode fail-loud specifically to avoid 'resurrecting the emitter 030f deletes'.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend 1c1b Decision D1 to state that 030f RETAINS the live BRIDGE_ALERT emitter/reducer, and rephrase the no-event rationale as 'strict mode adds no NEW alert artifact' rather than 'does not resurrect the emitter 030f deletes.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the authoritative upstream for the vendored GitLab CI schema (e.g. SchemaStore's gitlab-ci schema) and note that GitLab does not publish a standalone vendorable schema, so offline validation approximates rather than mirrors server-side lint.
evidence: Retrieved prior art: schemastore.org and github.com/SchemaStore/schemastore host the de-facto gitlab-ci JSON schema consumed by editors/validators.
Retrieved: GitLab docs 'Contribute to the CI/CD Schema' describe a schema that lives in the GitLab monaco-yaml pipeline, not as a standalone published artifact — so 'official' needs a named source.
ABSENCE: the plan records the metadata to capture (revision/URL/date/dialect/checksum) but never states WHICH upstream is the authoritative source of that schema.
findings.finding: The offline GitLab CI schema-validation AC requires a 'vendored official schema' but does not name the canonical prior-art source, leaving 'official' unanchored given GitLab does not publish a standalone vendorable schema file.
findings.location: Portability acceptance criteria: '.gitlab-ci.yml validates offline against a vendored official schema whose immutable source revision, URL, retrieval date, dialect, and checksum are recorded.'
scenarios: The implementer vendors a schema from an ambiguous source and a reviewer cannot confirm it is the intended 'official' one.
SchemaStore's gitlab-ci schema lags real GitLab keyword additions, so 'official' is materially different from GitLab's own validation.
